Susan / Michael — Laura here from Redwood Privacy. I reviewed the redline and SOC2 artifact. High-level assessment and recommended scoping options below.

Summary observations:
- SOC2 Type 2 is current and helpful; we'll still need recent penetration test summary and evidence of encryption-in-transit + at-rest.
- The redline requests for per-country residency + expanded subprocessors notice are reasonable but will drive either a contractual commitment plus technical isolation (Dedicated / Private) or a narrower scoping approach.

Suggested approaches (tradeoffs):
1) Private deployment (customer-controlled VPC or on-prem package) — strongest contractual/technical guarantee for HIPAA/GLBA. Customer-managed KMS/HSM, no shared tenancy. Best for EU residency requirement and strict BAA scope. Estimated ops timeline: 4–8 weeks for onboarding (infra + networking + legal).

2) Dedicated (reserved GPU pools with VPC egress controls) + contractual residency commitments — lower operational lead time (2–4 weeks) but requires stronger legal commitments on subprocessors, attestations, and a guaranteed fallback. Works if Everwell accepts some managed infra as long as data residency is guaranteed in region.

3) Hosted + contractual scoping (limited endpoints + strict subprocessor notice) — fastest but less suitable when you require full residency and customer-managed keys.

Immediate ask to move forward:
- Please confirm which of the three approaches maps to your risk tolerance for the two verticals (portal PHI vs lending GLBA).
- Share a list of exact endpoints or API paths that will be in-scope for PHI and for GLBA.

We will draft a DPA response that includes: an appendix with BAA language, a subprocessors table (with per-country locations), and a technical annex describing deployment options. Michael will own the MRP (mutual action plan) and scheduling.
